test.title: Motion in Two Dimensions - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: The maximum vertical height to which a man can throw a ball is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>136</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The maximum horizontal distance upto which he can throw the same ball is
A bead of mass m stays at point Pa, b on a wire bent in the shape of a parabola y=4Cx2 and rotating with angular speed ω (see figure). The value of ω is (neglect friction)
A bomb is dropped by a fighter plane flying horizontally. To an observer sitting in the plane, the trajectory of the bomb is a :

options.text: straight line vertically down the plane
parabola in a direction opposite to the motion of plane
parabola in the direction of motion of plane

question.text: The distance of the Sun from earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and its angular diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2000</mn><mo>''</mo></math> when observed from the earth. The diameter of the Sun will be

Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of \(\left(45^{\circ}-\alpha\right)\) and \(\left(45^{\circ}+\alpha\right)\), respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :

A child of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is going round a merry-go-round that makes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> rotation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The radius of the merry-go-round is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The centrifugal force on the child will be

A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a distance <math><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> from it. If <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the product <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is:
A particle is moving with constant speed in a circular path. When the particle turns by an angle 90°, the ratio of instantaneous velocity to its average velocity is π:x2. The value of x will be
The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is :

A disc is rolling without slipping on a surface. The radius of the disc is R. At t=0, the top most point on the disc is A as shown in figure. When the disc completes half of its rotation, the displacement of point A from its initial position is

A projectile is launched at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> with the horizontal with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. After <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, its inclination with horizontal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>tan</mi><mi>β</mi></math> will be : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>.

A player kicks a football with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> from the ground. What are the maximum height and the time taken by the football to reach at the highest point during motion? (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

A body of mass 10 kg is projected at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point 20,10. If T is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time t=T2, is _____ .
[Take g=10 m s-2]

Two guns <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>B</mi></math> can fire bullets at speeds <math><mn>1</mn><mi> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math><mn>2</mn><mi> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></math> respectively. From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is:

Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is :

A body is projected at $t=0$ with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at $t=1$ s is $R$. Neglecting air resistance and taking acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, the value of $R$ is:

The initial speed of a projectile fired from ground is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math>. At the highest point during its motion, the speed of projectile is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>u</mi></math>. The time of flight of the projectile is:

A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> projected with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> making an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> is :

A projectile is projected with velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> with the horizontal. After <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> seconds its inclination with horizontal becomes zero. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> represents horizontal range of the projectile, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> will be : [use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>use</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

The trajectory of a projectile near the surface of the earth is given as <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> If it were launched at an angle <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math> with speed <math><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math> then <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>:</mo></math>

Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the body was projected at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, with horizontal then sum of the maximum heights, attained by the two projectiles, is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

The projectile motion of a particle of mass 5 g is shown in the figure.

The initial velocity of the particle is 52 ms-1 and the air resistance is assumed to be negligible. The magnitude of the change in momentum between the points A and B is x×10-2 kgms-1. The value of x, to the nearest integer, is ___ .

A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ from horizontal at a speed of $60 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $\mathrm{h}_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0: h_1$ is _________
[Take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ]

A body starts falling freely from height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> hits an inclined plane in its path at height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math>. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mi>h</mi></mfrac></math> for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.

An object is projected in the air with initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math>. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____  degree.
